title: On the Convergence of Zeroth-Order Federated Tuning for Large Language Models

problem.claim: Fine-tuning large language models requires substantial memory, creating challenges for clients with limited computational resources.

gap.claim: The theoretical behavior and convergence properties of memory-efficient zeroth-order federated tuning for large language models had not been examined, including the role of large parameter spaces and critical convergence parameters.

contributions.claim: The paper integrates memory-efficient zeroth-order optimization into federated learning for LLM tuning, calling the approach FedMeZO.
The paper develops a theoretical examination of FedMeZO for LLMs, including optimization behavior, convergence properties, and critical parameters for convergence.
The paper proposes a personalized federated learning strategy that customizes client-wise learning rates using theoretical insights.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that this is the first study to examine the theoretical underpinnings of FedMeZO in the context of LLMs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that FedMeZO converges faster than traditional first-order methods such as FedAvg and reduces GPU memory usage during training to levels comparable to inference.
The authors report that the proposed personalized federated learning strategy effectively accelerates loss reduction.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated learning and large language models are positioned as relevant to privacy-preserving natural language processing.
The memory demands of LLM fine-tuning create difficulties for computationally limited clients.
The paper introduces FedMeZO by combining memory-efficient zeroth-order optimization with federated learning.
The study analyzes FedMeZO's optimization behavior, convergence properties, and critical convergence parameters for personalized strategies.
The authors report faster convergence and lower memory use, then apply the theoretical insights to personalized client-wise learning rates that accelerate loss reduction.

source_observation.claim: Memory-efficient zeroth-order optimization can be integrated with federated LLM tuning under client resource constraints.

interpretation.claim: Reducing optimization-time memory requirements may make federated adaptation of large models more feasible on limited clients.

application.claim: Consider zeroth-order or other memory-efficient optimization methods when federated model tuning is constrained by client memory.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which client hardware, model scales, or task settings support this application.

unknowns: Specific convergence assumptions, bounds, and critical parameter values are not provided.
The abstract does not specify datasets, model architectures, client configurations, or experimental measurements.
Details of the personalized learning-rate strategy and comparisons beyond FedAvg are omitted.
